best_for: Photographers on Windows or Linux who shoot RAW and want a free, fast editor in the style of Lightroom that never touches their original files.
description:
RapidRAW is a RAW photo editor written by Timon Käch, a developer and photographer from Lucerne, Switzerland. It is built with Rust, and the whole image pipeline runs on your graphics card, so the preview keeps up while you drag a slider.

You browse your folders in a library, rate, tag and compare shots side by side, then edit with tone curves, color grading wheels, masks, lens correction, noise reduction and retouching tools. It can also stitch panoramas, merge HDR brackets, stack focus and convert scanned film negatives. Every change is saved to a small .rrdata file next to the photo, and the original file is left as it was.

points.title: Free, with one optional paid service
points.text: The editor and its built-in AI tools, such as subject and sky masks and AI Denoise, cost nothing and run on your own computer. Large generative removals can run free on your own ComfyUI server, or on RapidRAW Cloud, which needs a sign-in and was listed at USD 14 a month at the time of reading. One switch in the settings hides every AI feature.

points.title: Wants a good GPU and plenty of memory
points.text: The developer tests on Windows 10, macOS 13 Ventura and Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, and strongly recommends 16 GB of RAM and a dedicated graphics card. Very old or weak GPUs may show glitches. When the GPU cannot decode a RAW file, RapidRAW falls back to the slower CPU.

points.title: Camera tethering skips Windows
points.text: Shooting straight into RapidRAW with live view and remote camera controls works only on macOS and Linux, and only in a separate tethering build that needs the libgphoto2 library. HEIC photos open on Windows and macOS but not on Linux.

points.title: Batch exports from the command line
points.text: The `rapidraw export` command renders one file or a whole folder without opening the window, using the edits in the sidecar files or a JSON file of adjustments you pass. It writes JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF, JPEG XL or a LUT, and can skip photos whose edits have not changed since the last export.

points.title: Windows installs per user
points.text: The Windows installers, for x64 and Arm64, install for the current user and can run silently. Up to version 1.6.2 there were also MSI packages that install for the whole machine; later releases dropped them.

points.title: No Mac build in this listing
points.text: RapidRAW also makes builds for macOS 13 or later and for Android, but this listing covers Windows and Linux only. On Linux it comes from Flathub, verified as the developer's own, for x64 and Arm64. Linux lists only the current version, while Windows keeps 17.

points.title: Version 1.7 changes how old edits look
points.text: Version 1.7.0 brought a new rendering engine, and the developer warns that existing edits, color grading most of all, will look different after the update, even though your slider values stay the same. If you are in the middle of a project, an older Windows version lets you finish it first.
